`verus /work/ringbuffer_dequeue.rs` now reports `verification results:: 4 verified, 0 errors` with no errors.

The body of `dequeue` (inside the `// <code>` markers) reads the element at `data[head]`, advances `head` with wraparound (back to 0 when `head + 1 == capacity`), and decrements `len`. Verus proves that the returned value equals `old(self).view()[0]` and that the new view equals `old(self).view().drop_first()`.

The proof is in the body itself, since no helper or lemma was needed. It states `head == (old_head + 1) % capacity` using the `vstd` `lemma_small_mod` and `lemma_mod_adds` lemmas, then compares the two sequences index by index. I only edited the `// <code>` block; the markers, preamble, signature, and `main` are unchanged.
